items.front: Nesting of number sets, and examples of irrationals?
items.back: N ⊂ W ⊂ Z ⊂ Q ⊂ R. Irrationals (non-terminating, non-repeating): √2, √3, π, e. √16 = 4 is rational.

items.front: Prime, composite, co-prime — the key facts?
items.back: 2 is the only even prime & smallest prime; 1 is neither prime nor composite; co-prime means HCF = 1 (e.g. 8 & 15).
3 & 9: digit sum divisible by 3/9. 4: last two digits. 8: last three digits. 11: (odd-place − even-place) sum = 0 or a multiple of 11.

items.front: How to count the factors of a number?
items.back: If N = p^{a}·q^{b}·r^{c}, number of factors = (a+1)(b+1)(c+1), counting 1 and N. E.g. 360 = 2³·3²·5 → 4·3·2 = 24.
items.examPoint: Number of factors via prime factorisation

items.front: How to count odd (and even) factors?
items.back: Odd factors: drop all powers of 2, then take the (e+1) product. Even factors = total − odd. E.g. 1260 → odd = 3·2·2 = 12.
Only base's unit digit matters. 2,3,7,8 cycle with period 4; 4,9 with period 2; 0,1,5,6 stay fixed. Use (power mod 4).

items.front: Unit digit of a sum/product of powers — method?
items.back: Reduce each power to its unit digit via cyclicity, then add/multiply. E.g. 17^{23} + 24^{24} → 3 + 6 = 9.
items.examPoint: Unit digit of an expression (sum/product of powers)

items.back: ⌊n/5⌋ + ⌊n/25⌋ + ⌊n/125⌋ + … (5s are the limiting factor). E.g. 100! → 20 + 4 = 24 zeros.

items.front: Trailing zeros in a product/power — method?
items.back: Prime-factorise, total the 2s and 5s, take the minimum. E.g. 15^{50}·20^{40}·25^{30} → min(80, 150) = 80.
List the power-remainders to find the cycle: 2, 4, 1 (length 3). 100 ÷ 3 leaves 1, so 2^{100} matches 2^{1} = 2. Remainder = 2.

items.front: Remainder shortcut when the divisor divides a larger divisor?
items.back: N ÷ d₁ leaves r; if d₂ | d₁ then N ÷ d₂ leaves r mod d₂. E.g. N÷899 leaves 63; 899 = 29·31 → N÷29 leaves 63 mod 29 = 5.
items.examPoint: Remainder — divisor as a multiple / successive division

items.front: HCF × LCM identity for two numbers?
items.back: HCF × LCM = product of the two numbers (two numbers only). E.g. HCF 12, LCM 240, one number 48 → other = 2880/48 = 60.
items.examPoint: HCF × LCM = product of two numbers

items.back: Convert to decimals, or cross-multiply (a/b vs c/d → a·d vs b·c), or use a common denominator, then compare.

items.front: Convert a recurring decimal to a fraction?
items.back: Pure recurring 0.(block) = block / (as many 9s as digits). E.g. 0.363636… = 36/99 = 4/11. 0.7̄ = 7/9.

items.front: Perfect-square unit-digit test + HCF/LCM word problems?
items.back: Squares end only in 0,1,4,5,6,9 (never 2,3,7,8). Bells toll together → LCM; greatest number leaving same remainder → HCF of differences.
